chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: Banner Band, Victor Spencer and Clayborn Williams's school band
summary: Joe describes the Banner Band of New Iberia with Victor Spencer and Bunk Johnson, and Clayborn Williams's boys' band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about Evan Thomas, The Black Eagle Band.
Yes, he played with the Black Eagles.
Where was that? In New Iberia?
Yes. How far was New Iberia from your home town?
New Iberia was... Let's see, I played in Opelousas... That's when I first went home and went to

Opelousas, which was forty miles from Baton Rouge. And New Iberia was fifteen miles from Opelousas, where I played. And Lafayette, Louisiana, was another place they played around. Well, that was one of your good bands. They had a band they called the Banner Band.
I said the Black Eagle. I meant the Banner Band. I'm sorry. I threw you off there. But you knew what I was talking about.
Yeah, that's the band that had a very fine trumpet player named Victor Spencer.
Bunk was in there for a while, too.

Yeah, that's right. That's how Bunk got... When Bunk quit playing music, he went back down there and worked at a place where they made tabasco sauce, in New Iberia. But yeah, he played with that band.
Were bands like the Banner Band and Clayborn Williams famous bands in Baton Rouge?
Clayborn Williams had that name... Clayborn Williams was a marching band, and he had all kids, all young kids there. He had a school down there.
I don't know, I think it was like a reform school, just almost like the Waif's Home in New Orleans that Louis went to. And he taught them, and he was a good
teacher, and he had a pretty good-sized band, maybe 18 or 20 kids.
